latest.title: Stop Invalidating CloudFront Caches. Version Your Assets Instead.
latest.description:
A common pattern after deploying a static site or SPA to S3 + CloudFront: ship new files, then run aws cloudfront create-invalidation --paths "/*". It works, but it's the wrong tool for the job, invalidations are slow (can take minutes to propagate globally), cost money past the free tier, and "invalidate everything" throws away cache benefits for users who didn't need a fresh copy.
The better pattern: never invalidate. Make your file names change instead, and let Cache-Control do the rest.
